newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euromarkets mark time ahead of U.S. election.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euromarkets mark time ahead of U.S. election.

text.p: European bourses were mixed and the dollar slightly lower against the mark in early European trading on Tuesday as the markets focus turned to the U.S. presidential poll and Russian President Boris Yeltsin's heart surgery.
The enforced wait for results from both events should keep activity thin, analysts said.

News that Yeltsin's operation began around 0400 GMT briefly boosted the dollar against the mark as the German currency is traditionally vulnerable to events in Russia. However analysts said traders then looked to square up ahead of the U.S. election and the mark recovered.
The markets were counting on re-election for President Bill Clinton and maintained Republican control of Congress, dealers said. But they warned a Democrat "clean sweep" could upset the dollar.
"All eyes fall tonight and tomorrow morning on what happens in the congressional elections," said Stephen King, deputy chief economist at HSBC James Capel in London.
"If Congress remains in Republican hands that's probably reasonably dollar-friendly, and if it goes to the Democrats it's probably a bit negative for the dollar," he said.
At 1000 GMT, the dollar was quoted at 1.5110 marks, down from late Monday's European level of 1.5142 but off an overnight low of 1.5075.

London, Europe's biggest bourse, was 13.0 points or a third of a percentage point down at 3914.6 and dealers said nervousness over the U.S. election was weighing on sentiment. British industrial output data issued on Tuesday was in line with forecasts appeared to have little effect on the market.

A mixed bag of company results provided little direction and few positive surprises to lift the cautious mood in London. Major retailer Marks & Spencer added to the downbeat tone with a disappointing set of first half figures which pushed its shares lower.

"Despite the early fall the underlying tone is OK. It was just a bit sloppy yesterday afternoon on worries about what will happen in the U.S. The market is a bit nervous and shares are just getting marked back a bit," said one trader.

In Frankfurt, German shares started bourse trade firmer after a stronger Wall Street close overnight but dealers said ahead of results from Yeltsin's heart operation and the U.S. poll volumes were expected to be small. The Paris bourse was also higher in early, cautious trade. Car parts maker Valeo dropped and CGIP jumped on news the holding company was buying a 20.2 percent stake in Valeo from Cerus, a French holding company controlled by Italian financier Carlo de Benedetti.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 9.25 points or 0.43 percent at 2,151.4 at 1000 GMT.
CURRENCIES AT 1000 GMT The dollar was trading at 1.5110 marks and 113.80 yen compared with late Monday's 1.5142 marks and 113.93 yen.
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was down 13.0 points lower at 3,914.6.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 9.25 at 2,151.4.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was up 11.16 at 2,683.02.
Gold was firmer in early Europe at $379.25, compared with $379.05 at the London close on Monday. Silver was unchanged at $4.82.
